title: Declare a device-width viewport in every full HTML document

facts.note: Candidate file kinds that can hold or build a full HTML document.
Vendored and generated trees are never scanned.
Content observer that detects a file containing/rendering/building `<html>` (vs. a fragment). Applies to every such document in scope, existing or new; not limited to changed files.
Detector findings: meta absent, content lacks `width=device-width` (alone suffices), or zoom blocked.

fires: An existing `.html` file containing `<html>` has no `<meta name="viewport">`.
A `.tsx`/`.jsx` layout rendering `<html>` declares a viewport whose content lacks `width=device-width` (zoom otherwise allowed).
A `.ts`/`.js` template building a full document sets `user-scalable=no` or `maximum-scale` below 2.
A `.tsx` layout renders `<html>` with other meta tags but no viewport meta.
doesNotFire: An HTML fragment or partial template with no `<html>` element.
A JSX layout whose viewport meta is present with `content={VIEWPORT}` (only presence is judged).

given: Any full HTML document in scope: an `.html`/`.htm` file, a `.tsx`/`.jsx` layout rendering `<html>`, or a `.ts`/`.js` template building one
when: the document exists in the repository (new or existing)
then: The document declares `<meta name="viewport">` whose content sets `width=device-width`.
prefer: Declare `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` in each full document and keep zoom available.
During GREEN: add or correct the single viewport declaration in the document/layout that serves the current behavior.
During GREEN: reuse the existing shared layout when one owns the document head.
avoid: Blocking zoom (MUST NOT): `user-scalable=no` or a `maximum-scale` below 2.
unless: Fragments that are not full documents (no `<html>`) are out of scope.
Viewport `content` given as a JSX expression (`content={VIEWPORT}`): the meta must be present; its value is not judged.
why: Without a device-width viewport a phone renders a zoomed-out desktop layout, whatever the CSS says. Blocking zoom fails users who need to enlarge text, also an accessibility failure.
evidence: The full document declares device width (`width=device-width`) in its viewport meta and permits zoom.
verifier_detail: Scope: `.html`/`.htm` files, `.tsx`/`.jsx` layouts that render `<html>`, `.ts`/`.js` templates that build a full document; files without `<html>` are fragments and skipped. All in-scope documents are checked, not only changed ones.
Fail when `<meta name="viewport">` is absent, or its content lacks `width=device-width`, or contains `user-scalable=no`, or a `maximum-scale` value below 2. Each condition alone is a finding.
If `content` is a JSX expression (`content={...}`), it cannot be read statically: require presence of the meta only, do not judge the value.
audit: Original name/summary: Every HTML document declares a device-width viewport and allows zoom.

splitSuggestion.then: A full HTML document's viewport meta MUST NOT block zoom with `user-scalable=no` or a `maximum-scale` below 2.

sharedNodes.text: frontend_settings: `atdd-bun.yaml` → `frontend.viewports` (the widths responsive specs render at; the smallest bounds fixed widths) and `frontend.breakpoints` (the widths media queries may use).

additions.text: The source statement bundles two obligations (declare a device-width viewport; do not block zoom). `then` keeps only the device-width obligation; the zoom prohibition stays coder-facing as avoid[1] (MUST NOT) and should become separate convention `coder.bun.viewport-allows-zoom`.
additions.justification: Rule 2: one obligation in then; declare the split.

additions.text: "the document exists in the repository (new or existing)"
additions.justification: The output shape requires a when clause; the source's requirement is universal over every full document, so the trigger is phrased to impose no narrowing.

additions.text: fires/doesNotFire concrete examples and detector finding names
additions.justification: Illustrations derived directly from the source statement and exceptions; required by the output shape. Finding names are labels for the source's failure conditions.

trace.note: Zoom prohibition kept as avoid[1] (MUST NOT) and proposed as split convention.
